questions.subject: Karnataka Budget
questions.question: What is a state budget?

options.A: The annual statement of estimated government receipts and expenditure for the financial year, laid before the state legislature under Article 202
options.B: A statement of GSDP growth projections laid before Parliament under Article 110
options.C: A monthly report of actual audited expenditure submitted to the RBI
options.D: A document listing only the state's tax rates approved by the GST Council

questions.explanation: A state budget is the annual statement of estimated government receipts and expenditure for the financial year, laid before the state legislature under Article 202 of the Constitution.
questions.source: Karnataka Budget FDA/SDA Notes 11.5, Section A

questions.subject: Karnataka Budget
questions.question: What is the difference between BE, RE and actuals?

options.A: BE is the audited result; RE is the initial forecast; actuals are the updated forecast
options.B: BE is the initial forecast; RE is the updated forecast during the financial year; actuals are realised audited or recorded results after the year
options.C: BE and RE are identical; actuals are always lower than BE
options.D: BE is the Revised Estimate; RE is the Budget Estimate; actuals are provisional half-year data

questions.explanation: BE is the initial forecast; RE is the updated forecast during the financial year; actuals are realised audited or recorded results after the year. BE must not be treated as actual collections.
questions.source: Karnataka Budget FDA/SDA Notes 11.5, Section A

options.D: They are two names for the same indicator

questions.explanation: The budget measures government finances; GSDP measures the value of final goods and services produced in the state economy.

questions.question: What is a grant-in-aid?

options.C: A market borrowing instrument issued through RBI auctions

options.A: ₹1,85,025 crore: salaries ₹90,557 crore; pensions ₹41,136 crore; interest ₹53,332 crore
options.B: ₹1,85,025 crore: salaries ₹53,332 crore; pensions ₹90,557 crore; interest ₹41,136 crore

questions.explanation: Committed expenditure in 2026-27 BE is ₹1,85,025 crore: salaries ₹90,557 crore; pensions ₹41,136 crore; interest ₹53,332 crore.
questions.source: Karnataka Budget FDA/SDA Notes 11.5, Section E

questions.subject: Karnataka Budget
questions.question: What share of revenue receipts is committed expenditure in 2026-27 BE?

options.A: About 59%

questions.explanation: Committed expenditure is about 59% of revenue receipts in 2026-27 BE.
questions.source: Karnataka Budget FDA/SDA Notes 11.5, Section E

questions.subject: Karnataka Budget
questions.question: Why does a high committed-expenditure ratio matter?

options.A: It leaves less fiscal flexibility for capital projects and new programmes
options.B: It automatically increases the fiscal deficit beyond 3% of GSDP
options.C: It reduces the state's share in central taxes

questions.explanation: A high committed-expenditure ratio leaves less fiscal flexibility for capital projects and new programmes.
questions.source: Karnataka Budget FDA/SDA Notes 11.5, Section E

questions.subject: Karnataka Budget
questions.question: Is interest payment the same as repayment of principal?

options.A: No; interest is a revenue expenditure, while principal repayment is a capital financing outflow
options.B: Yes; both are treated as revenue expenditure
options.C: No; interest is a capital receipt, while principal repayment is revenue expenditure
options.D: Yes; both are financing transactions excluded from net expenditure

questions.explanation: Interest payment is not the same as repayment of principal: interest is a revenue expenditure, while principal repayment is a capital financing outflow.
questions.source: Karnataka Budget FDA/SDA Notes 11.5, Section E
